final_draft.answer: As observed on 2026-11-16, the password policy for IAM users in our AWS account (111122223333) requires passwords of at least 14 characters. It does not set an expiry period, so these passwords do not expire.
final_draft.note: The approved answer and the live account setting disagree, and a reviewer needs to check this before the answer is sent. The approved answer (answer:245d1ee4-3e99-489e-8885-61b116f32331, owner security@harborlight.example, valid until 2027-11-16) says passwords expire after 90 days. The live check of AWS account 111122223333 on 2026-11-16 found a 14-character minimum length but no expiry period, so passwords do not expire. I wrote the answer from the live check, not the approved answer, so it doesn't claim a 90-day expiry that isn't in force. The owner should decide whether to turn on 90-day expiry in AWS or update the approved answer. If expiry is turned on before sending, re-run the check and revise the answer. The live check also shows symbols are not required.
